A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same VRM study, with matching core equations, experiments and figures. v2 ends after the references; v3 includes supplementary Section 8. The supplied material supports a reliable comparison of documented content.

before.justification: v2 reports original VRM results on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, including CNN-to-ViT distillation, alongside pilot experiments and ablations.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification results and adds MS-COCO detection results and further experimental analyses in the appendix.

M1.justification: The principal graph construction, pruning rules and combined objective are retained. Section 8.7 adds a feature variant using pooled features instead of logits and explicitly removing Softmax. v2's logit-adaptor and normalisation discussion disappears, without establishing whether those extras were removed from the reported experiments.

E1.justification: v2 evaluates image classification on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, including CNN-to-ViT distillation. v3 adds object detection on MS-COCO train2017/val2017, substantially extending coverage to localisation and detection.

E2.justification: v3 adds CIFAR-100 comparators including NST, AB, DML, MGD and SemCKD in Tables 12–13, and RSD to the ImageNet comparison. TGeoKD and MLLD accuracy rows are removed; ImageNet also loses CTKD, NKD and FSP. VID, CAT-KD and PKT CIFAR-100 comparisons remain in the appendix. The timing comparison adds FitNets and CRLD and drops LSKD.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce Faster-RCNN-FPN detection with AP/AP50/AP75 metrics and 180,000 training iterations, additional CIFAR-100 model pairs, ImageNet augmentation comparisons, and a 360-epoch versus 240-epoch training control. Section 8.4 also newly discloses settings for retained experiments; this disclosure does not establish that those experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds tests of virtual-view supervision, longer training, temperature, separate pruning stages and feature versus logit inputs (Tables 11 and 14–18). Real ImageNet gradient examples, gradient-conflict measurements and logit-distribution analyses (Figures 4, 8–9) substantially extend the mechanism evidence. Existing component and batch-size ablations are retained.

E5.justification: v2 provides no repeated-run count. Section 8.4 of v3 newly states that reported results are averaged over three trials, without reporting seeds or between-run uncertainty. This establishes additional reporting, not an increase in runs.

E6.justification: v3 adds detection results of 35.46 and 32.67 AP, further CIFAR-100 results and numerous analysis outcomes. Existing entries also change: ImageNet ResNet34-to-ResNet18 changes from 72.93/91.03 to 72.67/90.68 in Table 2. The three VRM relation-encoder entries change from 78.76, 76.19 and 72.30 to 78.46, 75.30 and 72.10 (v2 Figure 7; v3 Table 7). The causes of these numerical revisions are unspecified.

T1.justification: The original KD, relation-graph and overall-loss mathematics and the IM/RM implication argument are retained. Several existing formulas receive equation numbers. The added entropy and optimisation discussions are qualitative explanations rather than new formal derivations, theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: The central contribution of virtual relations and graph pruning remains unchanged, as do the two headline accuracy examples. v3 explicitly extends the claimed applicability to MS-COCO detection and broadens the abstract's state-of-the-art claim across tasks.

C2.justification: v3 newly acknowledges that VRM trails FCFD and ReviewKD on detection and attributes this to the importance of fine-grained features. It also explains differing augmentation benefits on CIFAR-100 and ImageNet, advantages of logits over features, and pruning's relationship to gradient conflicts. These additions substantially expand mechanism interpretations and applicability qualifications.

D1.justification: The new appendix supplies pseudocode, augmentation-operation lists, optimisers, schedules, temperatures, image resolutions, hardware and implementation-codebase links, where v2 largely refers to unavailable supplementary details. v2's logit-adaptor/normalisation description and code/model release promise disappear. Documentation remains internally inconsistent: Section 5.5 specifies Huber loss, while Algorithm 1 uses MSE.

R1.justification: Section 8.7 adds substantial positioning against SSKD and HSAKD, distinguishing motivation, teacher retraining, matching objectives and augmentation choices. v3 also introduces references including RSD and removes TGeoKD. The detailed comparisons materially expand the rationale for VRM's novelty.

P1.justification: Much of the original prose and narrative order is retained. v3 condenses related work and method passages, separates Preliminaries and Pilot Studies into standalone sections, reorders analyses and introduces an organised appendix. The title, author contact details and some terminology are also revised.

P2.justification: v3 substantially reorganises the visual presentation: training curves move forward, the relation-encoder comparison becomes Table 7, and prediction maps, t-SNE plots and loss landscapes expand into appendix grids. Detection, pruning and augmentation tables and Algorithm 1 are added. Several original plots are reused unchanged within this expanded layout.

improvement.justification: v3 supplies training information missing from v2 and directly tests gradient mechanisms and transfer to detection, improving assessability and empirical support. The net gain is limited by removal of strong accuracy comparisons, inconsistent loss documentation, and broader state-of-the-art wording despite Table 3 placing VRM below FCFD and ReviewKD.
